thread.title: Apple’s sales warning puts pressure on the European luxury market - MarketWatch

author: Tonya Garcia
title: Apple’s sales warning puts pressure on the European luxury market - MarketWatch

organizations.name: lvmh moët hennessy louis vuitton se lvmh

text:
The European luxury market is taking a tumble in Thursday trading after Apple Inc.’s sales forecast cut ramped up concerns about the Chinese market for high-end goods.
Apple AAPL, -9.24% now expects first-quarter revenue of $84 billion, below previous expectations of $89 billion to $93 billion. The FactSet consensus is for sales of $85.47 billion. Apple is scheduled to report first-quarter earnings on Jan. 29.
London’s FTSE 100 index UKX, -0.62% took a tumble on Thursday following Apple’s announcement, and closed down 0.4%. Burberry Group PLC BRBY, -5.91% shares were down nearly 6% in Thursday trading while Kering KER, -5.49% whose brands include Gucci and Yves Saint Laurent, was down 5.5%, LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton SE LVMH, -3.63% was down 2.8% and Christian Dior SE CDI, -2.28% is off 2.3%.
See: Apple cut holiday sales forecast on iPhone and China weakness, stock falls 8%
“China is by far the most important player in the global luxury goods market with wealthy Chinese buying around $120 billion of high-end goods per year accounting for about a third of the global demand,” wrote Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at City Index by Gain Capital, a specialist in spread betting FX and CFD trading.
“But the ongoing friction with the U.S. is beginning to show its teeth and domestic economic indicators are showing a slowdown in the country’s manufacturing and services sectors, which is only one step from declining consumer demand.”
Concerns about the Chinese luxury market began to grow months ago, with HSBC analysts suggesting four stocks that are most likely to withstand any contraction in the Chinese market: Hugo Boss AG BOSS, -1.54% Tiffany & Co. TIF, -2.00% , Tapestry Inc. TPR, -3.55% and Capri Holdings Ltd. CPRI, -5.28% , which was previously Michael Kors Holdings Ltd.
Michael Kors became Capri Holdings on Jan. 2 , following its acquisition of Versace.
Tapestry, whose brands include Coach and Kate Spade, landed on Wells Fargo’s list of companies that it thinks will do better in 2019 than in 2018. Analysts said Coach is seeing sales and margins improve while expanding geographically, and both Kate Spade and Stuart Weitzman are taking turns for the better.
“All in, the news out of Apple might not be 100% applicable to all the brands in our space today... but at the very least this gives retail bears yet another reason to remain cautious towards our group,” Wells Fargo wrote in a separate note published Jan. 3.
See: Victoria’s Secret parent L Brands among 7 retailers Wells Fargo is backing in 2019
City Index casts a cautious eye on the positive spin President Trump has put on the possible resolution of talks between the U.S. and China, saying “the dispute between the two economic heavyweights seems likely to end up being protracted and painful.”
Apple shares are down 8.4% in Thursday trading, and down 16% for the past year.
“Given how intertwined the market is, it is only a question of time until the downgrade also starts affecting Apple suppliers, some of its competitors and luxury goods makers too,” City Index wrote.
The SPDR S&P Retail ETF XRT, -0.65% is down 10.1% for the last 12 months while the S&P 500 index SPX, -1.88% has fallen 9.2% for the period.
